dailyInsight.headline: Audit who owns every background result before a delegated child can finish
dailyInsight.insight: Hermes’ fresh process-handoff work makes a narrow but valuable operational rule explicit: a child’s background result should either be collected, stopped, or formally transferred to a parent that can receive it. Teams building delegated coding and CI workflows can use that rule to find progress messages that outlive the work they describe.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The public implementation moves a running child-owned process into the parent’s ownership under a registry lock, preserves a stated purpose with its completion, and reports unhanded child processes as orphaned before teardown terminates them. A focused test checks both the delivered completion and the disclosed leftover.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: Nested-agent systems often make a parent responsible for a result while leaving the child responsible for the process that will produce it. If teardown removes that process or hides its completion, a reassuring status message becomes an invisible stall. Explicit ownership gives an operator a concrete place to wait, cancel, or investigate.

actions.audience: Builders and operators of delegated coding, testing, or CI workflows
actions.label: Audit background-result ownership
actions.instruction: List every background process a child task can start, then verify for each one whether the child waits for it, stops it, or transfers ownership to a parent that receives its completion. Make the child’s final status disclose any process that will be terminated rather than leaving a parent to infer that it still runs.
actions.effort: 30–45 minutes for one representative delegated workflow

receipts.title: Hermes process-handoff implementation for child background work
receipts.supports: The public change adds a validated child-to-parent handoff, changes live process ownership and completion routing, caps transfers, and records child-owned work left for teardown.

receipts.title: Hermes delegation guide for handing a process to the parent
receipts.supports: The public guide says a child must wait, kill, or hand off background work before it finishes and explains that unhanded work is terminated rather than silently inherited.

receipts.title: Hermes subagent process-handoff regression test
receipts.supports: The focused public test demonstrates that a handed-off completion reaches the parent with its purpose while an unhanded sibling is named as orphaned before cleanup.

confidence.basis: A fresh public commit, user-facing lifecycle documentation, and a focused runtime test agree on the same ownership rule, but the reporting did not exercise an external CI provider or parent interruption.

dailyInsight.limitation: These receipts describe intended live-process behavior in one project. They do not establish production adoption, cross-platform reliability, checkpoint recovery, or what happens after the parent itself is restarted or interrupted.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if public source or tests show that an unhanded child process can safely deliver its completion to the parent after teardown, or that a handoff can leave the parent unable to cancel, inspect, or receive the transferred process.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for tests and release guidance covering parent interruption, restart recovery, long-running external watchers, and a clear operator record of which process owns a completion at each lifecycle boundary.
